Sr.
 Case No. : Fao No. 6613 of 2014
 Date of Decision : November 17, 2

National Insurance Company Limited .... Appe
 vs.
 Miss Suhasni and others ....

Resp
 Coram : Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Gurbir Singh.

* * *
 Present : Mr.Neeraj Khanna, Advocate
 for the appellant.

Mr. H.R.Bhardwaj, Advocate
 for respondent no.1.
 *

* *
 Gurbir Singh, J. :
1.

This appeal has been filed against the Award dated 31.03.2014, passed by learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Patiala (for brevity - the Tribunal) in the Claim Petition filed under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act (hereinafter referred to as - the Act).
2.

Respondent no.1 (hereinafter referred to as - the claimant) filed claim petition under Section 163-A of the Act, against respondents no.2 and 3 i.e. owner and driver of the offending vehicle (Alto Car No.HR-70-A- 4266) and the appellant - Insurance Company, seeking recovery of Rs.10 lakhs from the respondents along with interest as compensation on account of injuries suffered by her in the motor vehicular accident which took place on 02.09.2010 due to rash and negligent driving by respondent no.3.
2023:PHHC:146426 3.
Brief facts, as culled out from the paper book, are that on 02.09.2010, the claimant-respondent no.1 was going as a pillion rider on a scooty, which was being driven by one Sofia Behal.

The car bearing No. HR-70-A-4266, which was being driven by Ms.Seema Bansal-respondent no.3 and owned by her husband Mr.Parveen Kumar-respondent no.2 and insured by the appellant-Insurance National Insurance Company Ltd vs Suhasni And Others on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86601667/
1 Company, came and hit their scooty.

entities.text: Insurance National Insurance Company Ltd vs Suhasni And Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Both the riders of the scooty suffered multiple injuries.
The driver of the car alighted and tried to help both the injured but on coming of Vijay Kumar, she ran way and left the site of the accident.

4. Respondents no.2 and 3 contested the petition and filed their reply stating therein that a false FIR was registered against respondent no.3 and she had already been acquitted by the learned Trial Court.
In fact, no accident had taken place with her car.

The appellant Insurance Company filed separate written statement, taking objection that both the drivers of the vehicles involved in the accident were not holding any valid and effective driving licenses.
No such accident had taken place.

5. Thereafter, from the pleadings of the parties, following issues were framed :-
"1.
Whether the claimant has suffered injuries in a road side accident caused by negligence of the driver of car bearing number HR-70- A-4266?
OPP 2.
Whether the claimant is entitled to receive compensation, if so from whom and to what amount?
OPP 3.
Whether the driver of the vehicle involved in 2023:PHHC:146426 this accident were not holding a legal and valid driving license at the time of accident?
If so its effect?

OPR 4. Relief."
6.
Claimant herself stepped into the witness box as PW-1.
She also examined Karanbir Singh as PW-2, Santosh Rani as PW-3 and Nirpal Singh as PW-4.
Then she closed her evidence.
Respondents no.2 and 3 also tendered in evidence some documents including a judgment passed by a Criminal Court and closed their evidence.
Appellant-Insurance Company also tendered some documents in evidence and closed the evidence.

7. Learned Tribunal, on the basis of evidence led on the file, decided issue no.1 in favour of the claimant that she suffered injuries in a road side accident caused by respondent no.3 by negligently driving car bearing No.HR-70-A-4266.
Vide issue no.2, it was held that the claimant remained hospitalized from 02.09.2010 to 09.09.2010.

From the bills and discharge summary etc., it transpired that an amount of Rs.44,538/- was incurred by the claimant on her treatment and also an amount of Rs.23,816/- was proved to have been spent on medicines etc.
So, total expenditure on the treatment and purchase of medicines etc. was proved to be Rs.69,000/- (rounded-off).
Further, a sum of Rs.20,000/- was granted for pain and suffering.
Rs.10,000/- was granted under the head of special diet etc.
So, the claimant was granted a total sum of Rs.1,00,000/- as compensation.
It was held that there was no permanent disability suffered by the claimant.

8. Learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company has argued that the petition has been filed under Section 163-A of the Act, which 2023:PHHC:146426 is a special provision for payment of compensation on structured formula basis.

Under this provision, a Company is liable to pay only in National Insurance Company Ltd vs Suhasni And Others on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86601667/
2 the case of death or permanent disability.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd vs Suhasni And Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since, in the present case, there was no permanent disability and amount of compensation can only be granted based on the structured formula, the compensation awarded by the learned Tribunal under this provision is totally against the law.
9. Learned counsel for the claimant-respondent no.1 has submitted that the claimant was only a pillion rider.
The learned Tribunal has specifically held that the accident was the result of negligent driving of the car.
Mere mentioning of Section 163-A of the Act in the Claim Petition does not mean that the compensation could not be granted.

Reliance has been placed on a judgment of this Court in United India Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Ajay Matta and another - 2016(3) PLR 161, where the Court itself treated the petition as one under Section 166 of the Act and upheld the Award.

entities.text: United India Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Ajay Matta and another - 2016(3) PLR 161
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Learned counsel has also relied upon a judgment of Hon'ble Andhra Pradesh High Court at Hyderabad in case of Dadi Komuravva and others vs. Garshe Buchaiha and others - 2015 ACJ 1634.
10.

entities.text: Andhra Pradesh High Court at Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: Dadi Komuravva and others vs. Garshe Buchaiha and others - 2015 ACJ 1634
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I have heard the submissions of learned counsel for the parties and perused the case file.

11. The Claim Petition has been filed on account of injuries received by pillion rider of the scooty, on the allegations that driver of the car in question hit the scooty and the accident was result of negligent driving of the driver of the car.
It has been so specifically held by the learned 2023:PHHC:146426 Tribunal.
Neither driver of the car stepped into the witness box nor any other witness has been examined during the trial of the case to prove that the driver of the car was not at all negligent.
At the time of accident, the claimant was only about 16 years of age and it cannot be said that she was having any source of income at that time.
It is not the case of respondents that she was having any earning at the time of accident.

Mere mentioning of Section 163-A of the Act in the petition, which may be by wrong legal advice, cannot frustrate the main objective of constitution of the Tribunal, which is constituted to award just and reasonable compensation to the victims of accidents.
Since the claimant was the only pillion rider, who suffered injuries on account of negligence of the driver of the offending car, so, she has been fairly awarded the compensation.
12. In case of Ajay Matta (supra), similar question came before this Court.

The petition was filed under Section 163-A of the Act but income of the claimant was more than Rs.8,000/- per month,
whereas annual income should be less than Rs.40,000/- to file petition under Section 163-A of the Act.
This Court treated the petition under Section 166 of the Act and compensation was accordingly granted.

13. In case of Dadi Komuravva (supra), it was held by Andhra Pradesh High Court as under :-
".....

It has to be seen that under sub-section(4) of Section 166 the Claims Tribunal shall treat any report of accidents forwarded to it under sub- section(6) of Section 158 as an application for compensation under this Act.
Thus, a report of 2023:PHHC:146426 accident forwarded to the Tribunal under sub- section(6) of Section 158 is to be treated as an application for compensation.
There is nothing to say that such report should be treated as an application under Section 166 of the Act.
It can be treated as an application either under Section 166 or under Section 163-A of the Act.

Irrespective of section of law or a particular rule under which an application National Insurance Company Ltd vs Suhasni And Others on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86601667/
3 has been made the Tribunal has to award just and reasonable compensation.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd vs Suhasni And Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If it appears to the Tribunal that it would be just and reasonable to award compensation under Section 163-A the Tribunal may treat an application even under Section 166 of the Act as an application filed under Section 163-A and award just and reasonable compensation.
The object of the Act is to award just and reasonable compensation to the claimants.
No claim shall be rejected merely on the ground that the claim is made under incorrect section of law.

The ultimate object should be to render complete justice to the parties."
14.
The petition under Section 163-A of the Act is treated as petition under Section 166 of the Act.
Since the accident was result of negligent driving of car, so, the claimant is entitled for compensation under Section 166 of the Act.
The claimant has duly proved her hospitalization and medical expenses incurred by her on her treatment.

Therefore, keeping in view the expenditure incurred by her, the learned Tribunal has rightly awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.1,00,000/- which included Rs.70,000/- for medical expenses, Rs.20,000/- on account of pain and 2023:PHHC:146426 suffering and Rs.10,000/- for special diet etc.
15.
In view of what has been discussed above, I do not find any illegality in the impugned Award passed by learned Tribunal so as to warrant any interference at the hands of this Court.
16. Accordingly, the present appeal is without any merit and the same is hereby dismissed.
17. Pending applications, if any, shall stand disposed of along with this judgment.
November 17, 2023 (GURBIR SINGH)
